title: Documentation and Prior Authorization Standard for the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
Documentation and Prior Authorization unit standard for the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program: written orders, prior authorization, authorization grants, activation, denials and clinical documents.

## 1. The written order

1.1 Every shipment rests on a written order from the treating prescriber that names the item, the billing units per 30 days, the order date and the prescriber's NPI.

1.2 The order is valid for the written order validity (in calendar months) counted from its order date. The valid-through date is the day before the same calendar day that many months later (falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist), and Larkfield records that valid-through date when the order is received.

*Worked example (hypothetical).* With a 12-month validity, an order dated 10 March of a hypothetical year is valid through 9 March of the following year.

## 2. Prior authorization on tiers that require it

2.1 On tiers where prior authorization is required, Larkfield submits a prior authorization request to the payer once the written order is on file and moves the program from referral received to pending authorization.

2.2 *Retired clause.* As originally written, this standard provided, for every payer approval, that the payer's approval is recorded as an authorization grant with basis payer prior authorization, carrying the payer's PA reference, the approved units and the approved span, which runs the tier's prior authorization validity period in calendar months from the decision date unless the payer's approval states an earlier valid-through date, in which case the payer's date governs. That unqualified wording is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis, which treats one case separately: a new written order of the item that changes the CGM model while the payer authorization the program's latest refill of the item drew on is still in force has its grant recorded by Larkfield itself under that authorization's PA reference, without a new payer approval. Every other payer approval continues to be recorded on exactly the terms just quoted.

2.3 A prior authorization request is submitted as expedited only when the prescriber states on the order that waiting the standard decision time could seriously jeopardize the patient's life or health; otherwise it is standard. The payer is expected to decide within the tier's standard decision time (calendar days) of a standard request or the tier's expedited decision time (hours) of an expedited one.

2.4 A renewal request for a prior authorization may be submitted no earlier than the tier's renewal lead time, in calendar days, before the valid-through date of the authorization it renews, counted backward in calendar days from that valid-through date with the earliest submission day itself allowed, and it requires a written order that is valid beyond that valid-through date.

| Renewal lead time 30 days, authorization valid through 30 June (hypothetical) | Submission allowed |
|---|---|
| Submitted 30 May | No, earlier than the earliest submission day |
| Submitted 31 May, the thirtieth calendar day before 30 June | Yes, the earliest submission day itself is allowed |
| Submitted 15 June, with a written order valid through the following March | Yes |
| Submitted 15 June, with the only written order valid through 30 June | No, the order is not valid beyond the valid-through date |

## 3. Grants on tiers without prior authorization

3.1 *Retired clause.* As originally written, this standard provided, for every tier where prior authorization is not required, that Larkfield records the authorization grant itself on the basis of the written order (basis written order, or self-pay order on the self-pay tier), valid from the order date through the order's valid-through date, for the billing units the order covers within that span. That unqualified wording is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis, which treats one case separately: a renewal written order for the CGM supply allowance (A4239) on the CGM Original Medicare Program still receives its grant on the basis of the written order over the same span, but the units it carries are counted by the rule for such renewals. Every other authorization grant on a tier without prior authorization continues to be recorded on exactly the terms just quoted.

## 4. Activation, denials and clinical documents

4.1 A program is activated only when an authorization grant on file for the program is valid on the activation date.

4.2 A payer denial of a prior authorization is recorded with the payer's denial reason; the program stays in pending authorization while the prescriber supplies further documentation or a new request is made, and it closes only under the program's hold and closure rules.

4.3 Clinical documents are recorded with the purpose they serve and the visit date they document, and a document serves only the purpose recorded on it.

## 5. Points of judgement

- The written order, the authorization grant and the program status are all read from Larkfield's records: an order or grant the customer describes but that is not on file does not satisfy 1.1 or 4.1.
- A grant whose span has ended before the activation date does not activate the program, even though it is on file.
